title: Swedish meatballs
subtitle: Beef and pork meatballs in a cream and dill gravy
excerpt: Swedish meatballs are small, tightly packed beef and pork balls seasoned with allspice and nutmeg, browned in butter, then finished in a cream and beef-stock gravy with a little dill. They are served over egg noodles or mashed potato. An American comfort-food classic via Scandinavian immigration.
sourceNotes: Swedish-American culinary tradition. The Swedish meatball became a fixture of the American home-cooking repertoire in the mid-twentieth century, appearing in Joy of Cooking and similar mid-century American cookbooks. The original Swedish köttbulle uses allspice and is associated with Swedish home cooking from at least the nineteenth century.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze cooked meatballs without the sauce for up to 3 months. Make the sauce fresh when reheating.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the recipe easily. Meatballs keep in the fridge for 3 days.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Roll and refrigerate the uncooked meatballs up to a day ahead.

content.text: Swedish meatballs are small, dense balls of seasoned beef and pork mince browned in butter until deep golden, then finished in a pan sauce of beef stock, cream, and a little dill. Allspice and nutmeg are what distinguish them from Italian-style meatballs. The texture is firm and the flavour is mild but savoury.

Combine {{beef-mince}} of beef mince, {{pork-mince}} of pork mince, the soaked breadcrumbs, the beaten egg, {{onion}} grated onion, {{allspice}} of allspice, nutmeg, salt, and pepper. Mix well. Roll into balls about 3 cm in diameter. You should get about 24.

Melt {{unsalted-butter}} of butter in the wide frying pan over medium-high heat. Brown the meatballs in two batches, turning regularly, for about 5 minutes until golden all over and cooked through. Remove and set aside.

Pour {{stock-beef}} of beef stock into the pan, scraping up any browned bits. Stir in {{double-cream}} of double cream, {{dijon-mustard}} of Dijon mustard, and {{worcestershire-sauce}} of Worcestershire sauce. Simmer for 3 minutes until slightly thickened. Return the meatballs to the pan and coat in the sauce. Stir in the dill. Serve over egg noodles.

items.cause: Not enough binder, or rolled too loosely.
items.fix: Make sure the breadcrumbs are properly soaked in milk and mix the meat thoroughly. Roll firmly. Refrigerate for 30 minutes before cooking if they are very soft.

items.cause: Stock not reduced before adding cream.
items.fix: Boil the stock for 2 minutes before adding the cream to reduce and concentrate it.

content.text: All-beef meatballs are leaner and benefit from an extra tablespoon of soured cream in the mix. A spoonful of redcurrant or lingonberry jam stirred into the sauce at the end is the traditional Swedish accompaniment. Serve with mashed potato instead of noodles for a more substantial plate.

Swedish meatballs came to America with Nordic settlers in the 1800s and became a staple of the mid-century dinner table. They differ from Italian meatballs: smaller, milder, spiced with allspice not garlic, served in cream not tomato sauce.
